title: What a Transaction Hash (TXID) Is
summary: Every confirmed transaction gets a unique identifier called a transaction hash, or TXID — a long string that acts as its receipt.
blocks: Every confirmed transaction gets a unique identifier called a transaction hash, or TXID — a long string that acts as its receipt.
You can paste it into a block explorer to see the transaction's status, amount, sender, recipient and confirmations.
It is the definitive way to check whether a transfer actually happened, which is far more reliable than a screenshot someone shows you.
